nodes.description: The OST complex transfers the lipid-linked glycan en bloc to asparagine in nascent polypeptides in the ER lumen. The yeast orthologue of OST48, WBP1, is required for this transfer activity. Reduced OST48 is therefore expected to lower OST activity. How OST48 loss affects the assembly or stability of the human complex, and whether OST-A and OST-B are affected equally, has not been measured in patient cells; the step is inferred from the yeast data and from the hypoglycosylation that follows.

nodes.description: Cultured fibroblasts from patients are where the glycosylation defect, reduced DDOST protein and rescue by wild-type DDOST were shown.

Glycoproteins leave the ER with unoccupied N-glycosylation sites. This is seen as reduced glycosylation of cellular markers (ICAM-1, LAMP2) in patient fibroblasts and as a type I serum transferrin pattern. Plasma N-glycan profiling in one patient also showed mildly increased small high-mannose glycans, a pattern reported in other OST-subunit defects.
